panel.introduction: Earth (our home planet) is the third planet from the Sun, and the fifth largest planet. It’s the only place we know of inhabited by living things.

controls.label: Visible color
controls.description: NASA Blue Marble, December 2004, with an archival cloud composite. These global observations are not live imagery.
controls.title: Blue Marble Next Generation
controls.summary: NASA Blue Marble, December 2004, with an archival cloud composite. These global observations are not live imagery.

controls.label: Elevation
controls.description: GEBCO_2026 terrain model. Colors show meters above and below mean sea level; relief is shaded for readability. Ocean depths combine measured and estimated terrain. Land includes the ice surface.
controls.title: GEBCO land and seafloor heights
controls.summary: GEBCO_2026 modeled terrain. Colors show height and depth relative to mean sea level; ocean depths include estimates.
controls.legendNote: 0 = mean sea level. Shading emphasizes relief; the color scale is unshaded. Some coastal source datums differ.

controls.label: Night lights
controls.description: NASA Black Marble 2016 night-light composite. This archival observation does not depict current lighting.
controls.title: Black Marble night-light composite
controls.summary: Artificial lighting is combined from observations taken in 2016. The composite does not show present-day lighting.

controls.label: ENSO
controls.title: ENSO: sea-surface temperature anomalies · 7 Sept 2026
controls.description: NASA MUR · 1 km source imagery · 7 Sept 2026. Sea-surface temperature departure from the 2003–2014 average. NASA colors saturate below −3 and at +3 °C. Gray: land, ice, or unavailable imagery.
controls.legendNote: NASA imagery uses 0.1 °C color bins; the NOAA advisory describes the coupled ocean–atmosphere state.

controls.label: Cross section
controls.description: Schematic interior based on NASA Science. Layer boundaries and colors illustrate the model; this is not direct interior imaging.
controls.title: Interior structure model
controls.summary: Schematic Earth interior based on NASA Science. Colors and interior shading illustrate inferred layers, not photographs. Shadows changes the exterior lighting.

controls.label: Mantle tomography
controls.description: GLAD-M35 (2024) seismic model. Mantle colors show slower and faster vertically polarized shear waves relative to the global mean at the same depth. Crust and core are schematic.
controls.title: GLAD-M35 mantle tomography
controls.summary: Mantle shear-wave speed: % from the global mean at the same depth. Red is slower; blue is faster. Gray: outside the 10–2,890 km model. Crust and core are schematic. This is not temperature.
controls.legendNote: GLAD-M35 r0.1 · 10–2,890 km depth · 1° / 10 km sample grid. Gray: outside model depth coverage. Grid spacing is not resolving power.

charts.alt: NASA PSG modeled disk reflectance of Earth from 350 to 1000 nanometers.
Earth V-band brightness change across phase angles from zero to 180 degrees.
NASA PSG standard Earth atmospheric temperature and pressure profile.

charts.title: Earth modeled disk reflectance
charts.description: Complete 127-point NASA PSG Earth spectrum from 350 to 1000 nanometers at resolving power 120.

charts.title: Earth temperature-pressure profile
charts.description: NASA PSG standard Earth atmosphere profile. Pressure decreases upward on a logarithmic scale.

charts.title: Earth photometric phase curve
charts.description: V-band dimming of Earth as phase angle increases from zero to 180 degrees.

source.title: Computing Apparent Planetary Magnitudes for The Astronomical Almanac
source.qualification: V-band phase equations transcribed from equations 2 through 17. Distance, rotation, season, latitude, and ring terms cancel or are held fixed so each curve isolates phase-angle dependence.

metadata.measurement: V-band magnitude change relative to zero-degree phase

parameters.reference: Area-weighted horizontal mean of Vsv at each source depth, excluding the duplicated longitude endpoint. This display reference is not STW105, the inversion's reference model.
parameters.quantity: 100 * (Vsv / mean Vsv at the same depth - 1)
parameters.interpretation: Seismic inverse model, not a photograph or temperature measurement. Smooth interpolation does not add resolving power. Only the mantle portion of the schematic geometry is sampled; depths outside 10–2890 km are gray. Crust and core remain schematic.
parameters.longitudeSeam: Average the coincident -180/+180 degree source samples before periodic sampling; their maximum published difference is 0.080645084 km/s, at 20 km depth and 55 degrees north.

products.label: Normal
products.process: Prepare the global reference map and its declared cloud composite.
limitations: NASA Blue Marble Next Generation December 2004 with a prepared archival cloud composite

products.label: Topography
products.process: Decode signed terrain heights and coordinate axes, interpolate elevations, apply the authored palette and cartographic relief, and prepare the globe, minimap and unshaded legend.
limitations: GEBCO_2026 terrain model. Colors show meters above and below mean sea level; relief is shaded for readability. Ocean depths combine measured and estimated terrain. Land includes the ice surface.

products.label: Night lights
products.process: Prepare the global reference map and its declared cloud composite.

products.label: ENSO
products.process: Prepare the global reference map and its declared cloud composite.
limitations: NASA MUR · 1 km source imagery · 7 Sept 2026. Sea-surface temperature departure from the 2003–2014 average. NASA colors saturate below −3 and at +3 °C. Gray: land, ice, or unavailable imagery.

products.label: Cross section
limitations: Schematic interior based on NASA Science. Layer boundaries and colors illustrate the model; this is not direct interior imaging.

products.label: Mantle tomography
products.process: Sample pinned mantle velocities on the cut planes and shell; normalize by the area-weighted depth mean and bake the signed palette. Keep crust and core schematic.
limitations: GLAD-M35 (2024) seismic model. Mantle colors show slower and faster vertically polarized shear waves relative to the global mean at the same depth. Crust and core are schematic.
